title: Variable valve timing, cam correlation and mechanical breathing
whatItIs: Cam timing controls when valves open and close. Incorrect timing or sluggish VVT changes cylinder filling, idle vacuum, misfire behavior and high-RPM power.
normalValues: When VVT is healthy, actual cam position follows command and airflow/load change predictably with RPM. Fuel trims do not usually scream in only one direction from pure cam timing error.
deviations: Low VE with normal-ish trims suggests mechanical breathing
Bank split trims can suggest cam timing difference between banks
P0011/P0012/P0016-style faults need oil, actuator, chain/belt and sensor checks
Sluggish VVT can appear hot or after dirty oil
influence: VVT faults are often misdiagnosed as MAF, fuel or catalyst problems because the engine simply cannot breathe correctly.
checks: Check oil level, viscosity and contamination
Compare commanded and actual cam angle if enhanced PID exists
Run compression/leak-down if graph suggests mechanical loss
